As they divide his clothing, Jesus prays for the very people putting him to death. Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. Luke records it as they gambled: And they parted his raiment, and cast lots. "They know not what they do" does not excuse the sin; it intercedes for the sinner. And the sin that put him there was ours too. He gave himself willingly — and the Lord who prayed for his executioners still lives to make intercession for sinners. This is the gospel: while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us — pleading mercy before we knew we needed it. That mercy is held out to you now: come, and receive it by faith.

"Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots" (Luke 23:34, KJV).

As they divide his clothing, Jesus prays for the very people putting him to death. "They know not what they do" does not excuse the sin; it intercedes for the sinner. And the sin that put him there was ours too.

He gave himself willingly, and the Lord who prayed for his executioners still lives to make intercession for sinners. This is the gospel: while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us, pleading mercy before we knew we needed it.

That mercy is held out to you now. Come, and receive it by faith.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: Father, Forgive Them: The First Word From the Cross
platforms.description:
The first recorded words of Jesus on the cross are not a cry of pain and not a curse on his executioners. They are a prayer for them.

"Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots" (Luke 23:34, KJV).

Notice Luke's timing: the prayer rises while the soldiers divide his clothes and gamble beneath him. Jesus intercedes for the very men driving the nails, in the very moment of the driving.

"They know not what they do" does not excuse the sin; it intercedes for the sinner. There is a difference, and the difference is the gospel. The sin that put him on that cross was ours too, and he gave himself willingly. The Lord who prayed for his executioners did not stop when he rose: he ever lives to make intercession for those who come to God by him.

In this piece: the first Word from the cross in Luke's own sequence, what the prayer does and does not say, and the mercy that was pleading for you before you knew you needed it.

While we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. That mercy is held out to you now. Come, and receive it by faith.
